topic: Demonstration of Soldering and de-soldering techniques adopted on PCBs and cables.
syllabus_extract: Demonstration of Soldering and de-soldering techniques adopted on PCBs and cables. Safety precautions to be observed while Soldering and De-soldering on PCBs and cables.
specific_objectives: 24.13.1.1 Trainee will be able to carry out workshop maintenance on aircraft cables and PCBs.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of soldering and de-soldering on PCBs and cables; Safety precautions; Instructor supervision
intro_questions: What are the primary safety hazards associated with hot soldering irons?
Identify the components required for a basic soldering setup.
Why is flux necessary during the soldering process?

topics: Soldering iron selection and temperature settings
Heating and melting solder on PCBs
Cooling and inspection of solder joints
development.content:
Soldering iron selection and temperature settings
Proper flux application techniques
Heating and melting solder on PCBs
Cooling and inspection of solder joints

topics: Heat sink application for component removal
development.content:
De-soldering techniques using desoldering pump
Heat sink application for component removal
Cleaning flux residue from PCBs
Inspection criteria for damaged traces

Safety precautions for fume extraction
Fire prevention measures in workshop
Proper disposal of solder waste
Personal protective equipment usage

summary_questions: Explain the correct sequence for applying flux before heating the joint.
Describe the immediate action required if a soldering iron tip oxidizes during use.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report on the specific safety precautions required when de-soldering high-density aircraft cables, referencing the next lesson on crimping techniques.

pft_rows.syllabus: Demonstration of crimping techniques adopted on aircraft cables. Safety precautions to be observed while carrying out crimping on aircraft cables.
